theory_content: A fast moving average crossing above a slow moving average can indicate rising momentum. A cross below can indicate weakening momentum. Traders combine crossovers with trend direction and volume to avoid late entries.

Bullish divergence appears when price makes a lower low but RSI makes a higher low. Bearish divergence appears when price makes a higher high but RSI makes a lower high. Divergence can warn of trend exhaustion.
When price range and average true range compress, markets can be preparing for expansion. Breakouts after compression often produce stronger directional moves, especially with volume confirmation.
